You are an impartial principal engineer adjudicating which of two competing Technical Design Document drafts is the better solution for a Jira spike. Authorship of both drafts is deliberately withheld from you; judge purely on merit. Do NOT edit files. Be rigorous and specific; do not hedge to a tie unless genuinely warranted.

## The two drafts (read both in full)
- Draft ONE: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-Zimmermann-Handover/b89d6c24-3a92-463d-b6b1-042c7902f4d6/scratchpad/draft-ONE.md
- Draft TWO: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-Zimmermann-Handover/b89d6c24-3a92-463d-b6b1-042c7902f4d6/scratchpad/draft-TWO.md

Both are candidate solutions to the same spike, SFCC-123.

## The spike's Definition of Done
"A technical design document is produced covering the Contentful integration architecture, content model requirements, locale setup, and SFCC-side build scope, ready to be shared with the incoming Contentful squad as a briefing artefact."
Tasks: (1) document the Contentful->MRT->SFCC integration pattern & data flow; (2) identify content types required for Sprint 1 AND Sprint 2; (3) define what SFCC consumes (APIs, content-model fields, rendering logic); (4) locale configuration aligned to the storefronts; (5) clarify the Accenture-vs-incoming-Contentful-squad handoff boundary; (6) flag blockers/dependencies before the squad onboards.

## How to judge
Score each draft on: (A) architecture accuracy, (B) content-model completeness for Sprint 1/2, (C) SFCC consumption detail (APIs/fields/rendering), (D) locale correctness, (E) handoff clarity, (F) blockers completeness, (G) briefing quality (self-contained, consistent, house-style), (H) FACTUAL ACCURACY & internal consistency. For a TSD that a downstream team will act on, weight accuracy and internal consistency heavily: a confident false statement is worse than an omission.

## Independently verify these code claims yourself (repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa)
Open the files and confirm what is TRUE of the current code vs what is merely a documented target:
- overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts (is the live data layer SSR-first? GraphQL? or browser-side REST?)
- Is there any publish-webhook receiver or GraphQL client anywhere in overrides/ or scripts/?
- overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts (how many Studio Experiences are registered, and which?)
- scripts/contentful/content-types/ (how many CDA content types exist?)
- config/sites.overlay.js (how many PWA sites and how many distinct locales?)

## Neutral ground-truth facts (verified from Jira, Confluence, and the codebase; apply equally to both drafts)
- Jira issue TYPES/STATUSES: SFCC-51 Story/Blocked; SFCC-111 Story/To Do; SFCC-55 Story/Tech design; SFCC-117 Story/To Do; SFCC-90 Story/In Refinement; SFCC-58 Story/To Do; SFCC-94 Story/To Do (Squad-B); SFCC-96 Story/To Do (Squad-B); SFCC-52 Story/Tech design; SFCC-82 Story/In Refinement; SFCC-203 Story/To Do; SFCC-190 Story/To Do; SFCC-204 Story/To Do; SFCC-102 Story/In Refinement; SFCC-195 Story/In Refinement; SFCC-67 Story/To Do (parent epic = Checkout Flow & Delivery); SFCC-173 Story/To Do; SFCC-160 Story/To Do; SFCC-162 Story/To Do. IMPORTANT: SFCC-14 (Returns & Refunds), SFCC-11 (Cart), and SFCC-10 (Z.immerse) are EPICS, not stories.
- Sprint schedule (repo .docs/memory/sprintScope.md): Sprint 1 = Homepage&Nav Part1 + Regional Part1 + Common UI; Sprint 2 = Homepage&Nav Part2 + Regional Part2 + PDP Part1 + PLP Part1; Sprint 3 = PDP Part2 + PLP Part2 + Cart; Sprint 4 = Checkout Flow & Delivery; Sprint 7 = Returns & Refunds. (So checkout content is Sprint 4, returns content is Sprint 7, cart is Sprint 3.)
- Locale ground truth (config/sites.overlay.js + contentfulMapping.ts): 10 PWA sites, 9 distinct Contentful locales (en [default], en-US, en-GB, fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE), backed by 8 SFCC sites (EU domestic = one SFCC site split into 4 single-locale PWA sites). config/sites.generated.js additionally lists en-AU as AU's Business-Manager-level locale, which the overlay narrows to en. The repo doc .docs/integration/02-contentful.md section 7 TEXT claims "Eleven active locales" and lists en-AU plus a separate en(EU); the Confluence ops page says 9. The canonical, code-backed answer is 9.
- Current code reality: the live Contentful data layer is browser-side REST (cdn/preview.contentful.com, include=2). SSR-first fetch, GraphQL Content API, and the publish-webhook receiver are described in docs as the TARGET but are NOT implemented in the repo. Only one CDA content type exists (shoppableImage). Exactly three Studio Experiences are registered: collection-hero, image-text, shoppable-image.
- Ops setup checklist (Confluence 318472193): COMPLETE = CI CMA token generated, setup:contentful, config:contentful, MRT TEST env, Studio app installed. INCOMPLETE = MRT env vars per tier, cache-purge webhook config, Contentful roles restriction, and "add CI CMA token as GitHub Actions secret".
- Product image ownership is genuinely UNRESOLVED: PWA TSD section 9 says all imagery incl. product is served from Contentful; the Product TSD says product images load directly into SFCC (no external DAM); code resolves product images from SFCC DIS; a dedicated decision page (DC002 Product Images Location) exists but is currently EMPTY.
- House convention (per the accepted sibling spike page for SFCC-122): no emojis; a draft carries a [DRAFT] title prefix + a draft banner + a draft label; no em/en dashes.

## Output
1. Per-draft scorecard across A-H (score /5 each + one-line justification).
2. A ranked list of factual errors / internal contradictions in EACH draft, with the specific quote.
3. A ranked list of each draft's unique strengths (things the other lacks).
4. Verdict: which draft is the better SFCC-123 solution, and why (2-4 sentences). State a confidence level.
5. Merge recommendation: if the best outcome is one draft as base plus specific content pulled from the other, say exactly what to port and in which direction.

1	# Contentful Integration Technical Design & Content Model (SFCC-123)
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Editorial and CMS content in the Zimmermann SFCC platform is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team. MRT (Managed Runtime, Salesforce's PWA hosting layer) acts as the integration layer between Contentful and the browser-rendered PWA storefront.
6	
7	| Direction | Flow |
8	| --- | --- |
9	| Inbound (Contentful to MRT) | Published content entries (hero banners, editorial modules, navigation, footer, announcement banners, size guides, accordion copy) delivered via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA) to the MRT SSR layer on every page render. |
10	| Outbound (MRT to Contentful) | Cache-purge webhook acknowledgements; Management API calls from CI for schema migrations. No content flows from SFCC back to Contentful. |
11	| NOT in this flow | SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly. All CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager. |
12	
13	Contentful is the sole CMS for all eight Zimmermann storefronts. SFCC manages commerce data (products, pricing, orders); Contentful manages editorial data (copy, imagery configuration, page layouts). They complement each other without overlap.
14	
15	## Integration Architecture & Data Flow
16	
17	Pattern: Contentful to MRT (Node/SSR) to browser, SSR-first for SEO/LCP.
18	
19	Architecture diagram: PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration) with CDA (published content, SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on post-hydration reads; public token safe in bundle), CPA (draft content, editor preview only, token server-side in MRT, proxied through an MRT preview endpoint), Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net, srcset/sizes/avif|webp), and Publish webhook to MRT /webhooks/contentful (clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish, HMAC-verified).
20	
21	### API surface & token boundary
22	
23	| Surface | Origin / Boundary | Token | Notes |
24	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
25	| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN (public, read-only) | SSR-first; browser hydrates from SSR payload. Safe to embed in bundle. |
26	| CPA (drafts) | MRT proxy only | CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN (server-side) | Editor preview via iframe postMessage. Never reaches browser. |
27	| CMA (schema sync) | CI host only | CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN | Never in MRT/bundle, build-time only. Never embedded, never in PR diffs. |
28	| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET (HMAC) | Clears SSR cache keys on publish. TTL fallback 60s SWR. Rejected and logged if HMAC fails. |
29	
30	Key behaviours confirmed in 02-contentful.md:
31	- SSR first. Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload, no CDA call on first paint.
32	- GraphQL for composed pages. Where a page assembles many entries, the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
33	- Live preview. When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on postMessage events from Studio.
34	- Asset delivery. Images come from images.ctfassets.net. The storefront generates srcset, sizes, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint. images.ctfassets.net is preconnected from the document head.
35	- SSR cache TTL. 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache, the TTL is the fallback if a webhook drops.
36	- CDN rate limit. 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic, risk only during burst republish events.
37	- Bundle weight. Rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
38	- No PII flows through Contentful.
39	
40	### Content Ownership (from 02-contentful.md)
41	
42	SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001).

126	### Error Handling & Monitoring
127	
128	| Scenario | Handling |
129	| --- | --- |
130	| Contentful CDA unavailable during SSR | Render the page without editorial content. Log the error. Commerce data (SFCC) is unaffected. NEVER block the page render on CMS availability. |
131	| Contentful entry field is null or missing | Component must handle gracefully with a null-safe default. No uncaught exceptions from missing CMS data. |
132	| Invalid HMAC on incoming webhook | Return 401 immediately. Do not process. Log the attempt. |
133	| Schema drift detected in CI gate | CI exits non-zero. Deploy is blocked. Developer must run npm run migrate:contentful before re-triggering. |
134	| Migration script fails mid-run | Contentful does not roll back automatically. Developer must assess partial state and write a compensating migration. |
135	| Preview API accessed from browser | Should be architecturally impossible, CPA is MRT server-side only. If a browser request reaches CPA, treat as a security incident. |
136	| Consent gating failure (Didomi) | Fail closed: no third-party scripts load. Affects Vimeo embeds in editorial content. See SFCC-106. |
137	
138	Graceful degradation is non-negotiable: Contentful being unavailable must never break the commerce experience.

31	## 1. Integration architecture & data flow [DoD-1 · Task-1]

33	**Target pattern** (per `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` §3-§5 and [Technical Solution Design, PWA](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585) §7): Contentful to MRT (Node/SSR) to browser, SSR-first for SEO and LCP.
34	
35	```
36	PWA (SSR, then CSR hydration)
37	   ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA)      published content, SSR + browser; public token, safe in bundle
38	   ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA)        drafts, MRT proxy only; token server-side, never in browser
39	   ├──► Contentful Images API               images.ctfassets.net, srcset/sizes, AVIF then WebP fallback
40	   ├──► GraphQL Content API                 composed pages, one request, field-projected
41	   └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful   HMAC-verified; clears SSR cache keys
42	```
43	
44	| Surface | Origin / boundary | Token | Notes |
45	|---|---|---|---|
46	| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | SSR-first target; held as an MRT env var so rotation is centralised |
47	| CPA (drafts) | MRT proxy only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (server-side) | Studio live preview via iframe `postMessage` |
48	| CMA (schema sync) | CI / local only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Never in MRT or the bundle; build-time only |
49	| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Cache purge; 60s SWR TTL fallback |
50	
51	CDN limit: 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token, absorbed by the SSR cache. Single Contentful Space, one environment per delivery tier (see §4).
52	
53	> **Current implementation vs target (verified in code).** The live data layer is `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`: two hooks (`useContentfulEntry`, `useContentfulEntries`) that fetch **browser-side over REST** from `cdn.contentful.com` (CDA) or `preview.contentful.com` (CPA) with `include=2` to resolve linked assets. ---

## Code verification results (ground truth confirmed in `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`)

Every check confirmed the neutral facts and settled the disputed claims:
- `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` — **browser-side REST**. Two hooks (`useContentfulEntry`, `useContentfulEntries`) using `useState`/`useEffect` + `fetch` to `cdn.contentful.com`/`preview.contentful.com` with `include=2`. **No SSR-first fetch, no GraphQL.**
- **No publish-webhook receiver anywhere** in `overrides/` or `scripts/` (grep for webhook/HMAC returned nothing). No `graphql.contentful.com` client; the only `createClient` calls are the REST `contentful` SDK (experience route) and `contentful-management` (CMA scripts).
- `experiences/definitions.ts` — **exactly 3 Studio Experiences**: `collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`.
- `scripts/contentful/content-types/` — **exactly 1 CDA content type**: `shoppableImage.js`.
- `config/sites.overlay.js` — **10 PWA sites, 9 distinct Contentful locales** (`en`, `en-US`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`, `en-CH`, `en-HK`, `en-AE`). `contentfulMapping.generated.ts` `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` matches those 9 exactly; `DEFAULT_LOCALE = 'en'`; `SFCC_PRODUCT_ID_FIELD = 'productId'`; `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENTS` exists. `sites.generated.js` lists `en-AU` as AU's BM defaultLocale (overlay narrows to `en`).
- `hotspotPopup.tsx` resolves product images from **SFCC via `useProduct` (`@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) + `disBaseLink`** — corroborating that product imagery leans SFCC, not Contentful.
- npm scripts referenced by BOTH drafts exist (`push:dev…push:prod`, `sync:contentful`, `setup:contentful`, `migrate:contentful`, `promote:alias`, `detect:drift`, `generate:contentful`, `sync:regional-config`). `contentful` dep is `^11.12.4` (Draft ONE's "SDK v11" is accurate).

The net: **Draft TWO's code claims are accurate to the line; Draft ONE describes the target architecture as if it were the current build.**

Draft TWO has **no internal contradictions** and **no false code claims**.

**Draft ONE only:**
- Detailed, accurate multi-tier environment/promotion pipeline mapped to real `push:*` scripts, plus the production-alias zero-downtime strategy and `promote:alias` flow.

## 4. Verdict

**Draft TWO is the better SFCC-123 solution. Confidence: high.** For a briefing artefact a downstream squad will act on, the decisive axis is factual accuracy and current-vs-target honesty, and Draft TWO is accurate to the line where Draft ONE repeatedly presents the *target* architecture (SSR-first, GraphQL, publish-webhook) and *unresolved* questions (locale count, product-image ownership) as settled current fact, while also contradicting itself internally.
